Three empires took a bite out of Poland-Lithuania in 1772, 1793 and 1795. After the third, nothing was left to bite. This map shows every cut.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth was among Europe's largest states. But its parliament relied on the liberum veto: one noble's objection could kill a law. Neighbours bribed nobles to use it, and that made meddling easy.

2/ First Partition, 1772: after the Bar Confederation lost its war with Russia, Russia, Prussia and Austria seized border lands. The Commonwealth lost roughly 30% of its territory. Prussia took the north-west, Austria the south.

3/ Poland answered with reform. The Constitution of 3 May 1791 gave townspeople political rights and separated the branches of government. Its neighbours saw a revived Poland as a threat, not an example.

4/ Second Partition, 23 January 1793: Russia and Prussia, without Austria, signed the deal at the Grodno Sejm after their troops had entered the country. On the map, only those two powers appear in the 1793 slices.

5/ Third Partition, 24 October 1795: after the failed Kościuszko Uprising of 1794, all three powers took what was left. King Stanisław August Poniatowski abdicated that November. The Commonwealth ceased to exist.

6/ Sovereign Poland and Lithuania stayed off the map for 123 years, until 1918. Poles kept the idea alive through language, literature and uprisings, and the borders of 1918 looked very different from the old Commonwealth's.
7/ Which cut mattered most: 1772, when the powers proved they could do it, or 1795, when they finished the job? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
